descriptionHtml:
Bug B18 · P1 · known

Many dates and times follow the device clock instead of server time (UAT 3.8): 'NEW TODAY', admit date, vitals date, task done time, transcript date; with a phone two days slow a held drug is stamped two days back and the next cleanup deletes it

Tickets: TFA-92584 ready for qa (UAT 3.8) · counts as a QA bug: yes · found on: local

Note: Root cause known (Daniela asked for server time on 10-03); the deleted drug, missing badge and wrong draft restore are new symptoms

Other cases of the same bug (counted once): TC-01/S08, TC-10/S22, TC-12/S23, TC-19/S19, TC-22/S23, TC-25/S24a, TC-02/S13b, TC-16/S25

Approach · EFS Empty & Failure States · S28 Kept-draft restore decided by time, both contexts: device clock 2 h behind or ahead of the server, and a kept draft 13 h / 19 h / 37 h old

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U10a Session expired mid-dictation: the dictation is kept, a sign-in prompt shows, and the dictation is available after signing back in. (UAT EFS state 10; TFA-94745 state 10)
  • U13 Nothing the physician dictated or typed is lost in any failure state. (UAT EFS Expected Result; TFA-94745 AC 3)
  • T2 No patient data is stored on the device to support offline use (minimal session cache only, per SOW): only the unsaved tail of a dictation is kept, until the server has it, and it is wiped on sign-ou … (TFA-94745 AC 7; TFA-92570 AC 7)

Test design technique: Boundary values (boundary) — Sit right on the edge of the rule (exactly on time / a minute late, empty, longest, most) and see on which side the behavior changes.

Given Standard fixture plus second charts; the harness sets the browser clock with Playwright's page.clock.setSystemTime (the server clock is untouched), writes chart timestamps on the server, ends sessions on the server, and writes or dumps IndexedDB 'roundcompanion-session-drafts' rows

When (a) Clock 2 h behind: the harness stamps the chart's encounterEditedAt with server now (as Quick Dictation does); the session ends; type a tail; sign in. (b) Clock 2 h ahead: keep a tail the same way, then save newer text for the same field from a second, normally clocked session; sign in on the first. …

Then (a) The tail is restored, although the device clock says it was written before the server's save. (b) The newer text from the other session stays; the stale tail does not overwrite it. (c) The old tail is not silently put into today's field (it may be offered with its date; …

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): From U10a/U13 and ground rule 3.8 (server time, not device time): (a) cp mustContain the behind tail; (b) cp mustContain the newer server text and mustNotContain 'ahead stale tail'; (c) cp mustNotContain 'old tail from an earlier day' in the Encounter box unless a date is shown with it (datedIfShown), and the storage dump after load has no row with savedAt older than server no …

Where it ran: local probes (multi-device probes); test method PW · Playwright script; lane planned in the matrix: browser agent (blocked)

S28 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/EFS.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Triage (2026-10-14): 0 rows.

Environment: local — main e02167f, local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane probes.

Test method: PW · Playwright script; secondary: TIME · Time / aging (clock moved) — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on local; Source: probes.

UAT item: EFS Empty & Failure States · Section: A5 · Cross-Cutting · Scenario: EFS/S28

Kept-draft restore decided by time, both contexts: device clock 2 h behind or ahead of the server, and a kept draft 13 h / 19 h / 37 h old

Tickets: TFA-92570 Mobile: Capacitor wrap for App Store & Google Play (ready for qa); TFA-94745 Empty & Failure States (ready for qa)

New local lane probes: status failed in probes/results.json → failed · product (failed · product (the lane flagged a product issue)).

How it is tested (probes/plan.json, automatable: yes): Scripted probe: (a) page.clock 2 h behind, encounterEditedAt stamped with server now, session ended, tail typed, re-sign-in, tail must be back; (b) clock 2 h ahead, stale tail, newer text saved from a second normally clocked session, newer must stay; (c) kept-draft rows written into IndexedDB (19 h / 37 h Hospital, 13 h NH) on charts whose encounter the sweep cleared, open each chart, old tail must not be silently in today's box, IndexedDB dump: no row older than server now - 36 h. [Review 2026-10-14] (a)/(b) add the tail in one input event (as S16) so it reaches the device copy (asserted as a setup check); (a) records the copy's text and savedAt vs the server stamp; (b) reads the stored field after the other session saved (setup check) and again at the end. — device-clock (page.clock), IndexedDB writes/reads and session-control are scriptable locally.

Detail:

Re-checked after review 2026-10-14 (18:00 JST runs: fix-*.json). (a) device clock 2 h behind, both contexts: the tail, appended in one input event after the session ended, reached the device copy ('QA-EFS-28 first line. QA-EFS-28 behind tail.', savedAt 2 h before the server-stamped encounterEditedAt) and was NOT restored: the box shows only 'QA-EFS-28 first line.'. (b) device clock 2 h ahead, both contexts: the device copy held the stale tail; the other (normally clocked) session's newer text was read back from the server ('QA-EFS-28 newer text from the computer.'), then after the phone signed in the server and the box hold the phone's old copy ('QA-EFS-28 first line. QA-EFS-28 ahead stale tail.'). (c) unchanged since 16:32: device copies 19 h / 37 h (Hospital) and 13 h (NH) old are put silently into today's Encounter box with no date; draft rows gone after load (restored, not expired) — same root cause as TC-25/S27 R, see productIssue part 2.

Product issue: 1) [draft-restore-device-clock] Mixed-clock case only: whether a kept device copy is restored is decided by the copy's savedAt (device clock) against the field's *EditedAt, and that stamp can come from another clock: server time (Quick Dictation, convex/quickDictation.ts:154) or another, correctly clocked device (client Date.now()). (a) Phone 2 h slow, field last stamped by the server: the words dictated after the session expired are dropped without notice — after signing in the Encounter box shows only 'QA-EFS-28 first line.' (both contexts; the device copy held the tail). (b) Phone 2 h fast: the server held the computer's newer text 'QA-EFS-28 newer text from the computer.'; after the phone signed in again, its old copy replaced it on the server and on screen (both contexts). A phone that is the only editor stamps device time on both sides and is not affected. Breaks EFS U10a/U13 ('nothing typed is lost', the tail comes back) and ground rule 3.8 (time-based state uses server time). 2) (c) is the same issue as TC-25/S27 R: [kept-draft-restore-after-sweep] Text the retention sweep cleared comes back from a device copy. What a physician sees: yesterday's pre-round text (past its 12 h window) or encounter text (past 36 h) reappears, undated, in today's field on the phone, is saved again (stamped now) and shows on the computer; in Hospital the encounter the sweep had already archived ('Oct 12 · Encounter notes') is re-saved as today's encounter as well. How such a copy is left behind in normal use: a device copy left behind after a normal save — e.g. leaving the field within the 0.8 s autosave (the unmount flush writes the copy and saves; nothing deletes the copy once the server has the same text: TC-25/S27 L-leftover, both contexts), or a Save Note that changes the stored text (TC-25/S17 b-hospital end-of-run row). Cause: the sweep clears preRoundNotes / encounterNotes (convex/lib/lifecycle.ts:124, :163 Hospital; :306, :329 Nursing Home) without moving *EditedAt, and useAutosave restores any device copy whose savedAt is newer than that stamp, however old (src/lib/useAutosave.ts:115-137; the copy's own age is never checked). Breaks UAT 3.6 (retention windows) and OAT-04 ('never survives past its window'); EFS U13 / S28 (c) (old text not silently put into today's field).

Evidence: 6 attached.

Dev run: skipped: local-only — local-only — Moves the browser clock, ends sessions with the sessions:_backdateForTests admin seam, signs in again with email codes, writes from a second session and writes IndexedDB rows: dev has no admin key, the runner never types a code there and must not end the shared saved sign-in (runner-contract §10.…. This local result replaces that dev entry (the scenario appears once).
